verdict: 🔴 Ship-blocker present. Sound, genuinely local-first stack undermined by the repo violating its own privacy promise (committed credentials/DBs, 0.0.0.0 bind, Windows-only launch). All red items are low-effort.
executive_summary: Haven is a local-first private-AI workflow engine (messy text → structured, risk-flagged JSON) at 2,778 LOC. The architecture is coherent — coordinator → router → 7 agents, a privacy/budget/content middleware tier, Qdrant vector memory, and a hand-rolled GitHub-dark dashboard — and the stack choices are correct for the mission (Ollama local + budget-capped Claude + Qdrant). The problem is repo hygiene and platform reach contradicting the pitch: live Gmail credentials, .env, owner PII and 5 databases are committed to git; the server binds 0.0.0.0; one-button launch is Windows-only while the repo runs on macOS. Fix the five red items (all S-effort) and Haven is demo-ready; the higher-value work is a Data-Access Layer and a graceful-fallback path.
